newsitem.title: USA: AT&T Corp sanguine about interconnection.
newsitem.headline: AT&T Corp sanguine about interconnection.

text.p: AT&T Corp said Monday that the results of arbitration for it to connect its networks to those of the local exchange carriers were producing results in-line with what the Federal Communications Commission had intended.
John Zeglis, AT&T general counsel, said that of 53 arbitration processes in 33 states, 27 had been completed, and of those, 24 had produced resale discounts within the FCC's 17 to 25 percent range.
"All 27 ordered full unbundling too," Zeglis told a Salomon Bros investment conference.

The arbitration process is used when incumbent carriers of local telephone service cannot agree on terms of interconnection with networks of new entrance into their monopoly markets. The process, which is binding, was mandated under the 1996 Telecommunications Act, which became law in February.
The discounts are measured from the retail rates charged to customers, and the resulting rate is the wholesale rate applied to new entrants who want to use the existing local network.
Zeglis said AT&T was having the most trouble in states in which GTE Corp provided local services.
"GTE is the high-cost company, and they can prove it," Zeglis said, referring to the more modest discounts that had resulted from arbitration in GTE areas.

The FCC was originally going to implement a 17 to 25 percent discount across the entire country until a legal challenge initiated by GTE and others, which has now thrown much of the responsibility back on the state regulatory commissions. However, Zeglis said that the results were not expected to be much different.
